title: Explore vs Execute: why the post-PMF company needs a different culture, team and mindset
summary: Jason Cohen argues that hitting product/market fit demands a radical shift from "Explore" (figure out what works) to "Execute" (become excellent at what works, at scale). The founder belief that "what got us here will get us there" is the trap. Roles, quality bar, risk, predictability and even which people fit all change, including the founder.

principles.text: After PMF, what got you here won't get you there; the company, and the founder, must change.
principles.quote: What Arrogant Founder doesn't realize is that the needs of the company dramatically change after Product/Market Fit. Everyone and everything at the company will change. Including the founder.

principles.text: Explore means finding what works fast; Execute means getting excellent at it while scaling. Applying the wrong one fails.
principles.quote: Prior to Product/Market Fit, you don't yet know what ought to be repeated, what should be excellent, and you have to discover and jettison whatever is wrong as quickly as possible.

principles.text: Executives must shift from building things themselves to building teams that build them.
principles.quote: Executive roles transition from building things themselves to building teams that build those things.

principles.text: Post-PMF, operations rather than business model is what kills you, so de-risking becomes the priority.
principles.quote: Before, the company was likely to fail because it hadn't figured out a business model that works, but now the thing that will cause failure is operations.

principles.text: At scale, rare problems become daily problems, so quality, requirements and process start to matter.
principles.quote: Before, a bug that affected 1% of customers didn't matter. Now it causes 5 support tickets every day, and mad customers who complain on Twitter.

principles.text: Hiring lag of six months or more forces predictability, playbooks and forecasting of future needs.
principles.quote: The time between deciding to open a position, and having a trained, productive person in that position, is at least six months.
